rv.q: Angela Carter hailed Kureishi’s novel for its humour and heart: this show comes with bundles of both.
Emma Rice's RSC production can't quite get a handle on Kureishi's big, brash 1990 debut novel about a mixed-race bisexual teenager, but it approaches the book with a colourful, playful touch.
But what's left is a lovable play, filled with deadpan humour and joyful theatricality.
It's very rarely that every single aspect of a production comes together so stonkingly well.
